c74object.name: evi_smooth
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_smooth.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_smooth.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
The evi_smooth.genexpr file also requires:
evi_utilities.genexpr
About this File:
A large collection of param rate and audio rate smoothing functions used all over evieve. Many are efficient inexact destination smoothers, others are more expensive exact destination smoothers. There is enough variety here to suit all the situations evieve needs from a technical and also creative (sound design) point of view. This .genexpr file also inherits 'evi_utilities.genexpr' and therefore 'evi_approx.genexpr' as well, so it gets required in many evieve abstractions and is a very useful all-in-one require for a lot of what we need to do in GenExpr.

entry.name: stepsmooth ( )
entry.description:
A GenExpr version of smoothstep()
In 1: type=input: x, Left edge value
In 2: type=input: y, Right edge value
In 3: type=input: a, Smoothly step from 'x'..'y' over this 0..1
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothly stepped value out

entry.name: polesmooth ( )
entry.description:
A simple onepole smoother. Like Faust smooth(), like 'expsmooth()' without the time compensation
In 1: type=input: x, Value to smooth
In 2: type=input: s, Pole range, e.g. 0.999 (must be < 1)
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothed output ramp

entry.name: cfSmoothLinear ( )
entry.description:
Signal smoother particularly well suited to smoothing cutoff frequencies. Based on Andy Simper's smoother, it tracks the input value via the bandpass output of an SVF filter and logarithmically updates. Smoothing is specified in both ramp time (seconds) and filter cutoff (Hz).
In 1: type=input: x1, Destination value
In 2: type=input: hz, Smoothing filter cutoff in Hz (typically 1..5)
In 3: type=input: s, Smoothing time in SECONDS
Return 1: Ramp, Smoothed output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete.

In 3: type=input: hz, Smoothing filter cutoff in Hz (typically 1..5)
In 4: type=input: s, Smoothing time in SECONDS
Return 1: Ramp 1, Smoothed output ramp 1, or target value 1 if ramp is complete.
Return 2: Ramp 2, Smoothed output ramp 2, or target value 2 if ramp is complete.

entry.name: cfSmoothCubic ( )
entry.description:
Signal smoother particularly well suited to smoothing cutoff frequencies. Based on Andy Simper's smoother, it tracks the input value via the bandpass output of an SVF filter and logarithmically updates. Smoothing is specified in both ramp time (seconds) and filter cutoff (Hz). This cubic version is much more expensive than the linear version and very rarely worth it.
In 1: type=input: x1, Destination value
In 2: type=input: hz, Smoothing filter cutoff in Hz (typically 1..5)
In 3: type=input: s, Smoothing time in SECONDS
Return 1: Ramp, Smoothed output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete.

entry.name: smoothCoeff ( )
entry.description:
Coefficients calculation for using a biquad as a smoother. Can optionally be computed entirely at param rate
In 1: type=input: smooth, Smoothing value in Hz, typically in a low range e.g. 1..10
In 2: type=param (optional): q, default: 0.54945, It is recomended not to change this Q value from the default
Return 1: a0, a0 biquad coefficient
Return 2: a1, a1 biquad coefficient
Return 3: a2, a2 biquad coefficient
Return 4: b1, b1 biquad coefficient
Return 5: b2, b2 biquad coefficient

entry.name: lagsmooth ( )
entry.description:
A bit like Supercollider lag3(), a bootilicious smoother. Complex ramp generator with smooth logarithmic curve that reaches it's destination within a threshold of -60dB.
In 1: type=input: v, Destination value
In 2: type=input: lp0, Ramp time in SECONDS
Return 1: Ramp, Smoothed output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete

entry.name: lagsmoothThresh ( )
entry.description:
Like Supercollider lag3(), a bootilicious smoother, more expensive version with variable threshold. Complex ramp generator with smooth logarithmic curve that reaches it's destination within a given threshold.
In 1: type=input: v, Destination value
In 2: type=input: lp0, Ramp time in SECONDS
In 3: type=input: th, Threshold for log() e.g. 0.001 = -60dB
Return 1: Ramp, Smoothed output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete

entry.description:

In 2: type=input: r, Ramp time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: p, Lin/log flag 0/1
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothed output ramp

entry.name: ramptwo ( )
entry.description:
Like the bastard twins of a 'rampone()' and 'logdecay()' tryst
In 1: type=input: x, Value to smooth
In 2: type=input: u, Ramp up time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: d, Ramp down time in SAMPLES
In 4: type=input: p, Lin/log flag 0/1
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothed output ramp

entry.name: eviLine ( )
entry.description:
Reimplementation of MSP [line~] algorithm as efficiently as possible. Exact destination ramp.
In 1: type=input: target, Destination value
In 2: type=input: duration, Ramp time in SAMPLES
Return 1: Ramp, Output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete
Return 2: Notify, 1 When Ramp Reaches Destination (0 During Ramp)

entry.name: eviSline ( )
entry.description:
Same as 'eviLine()' but with an S-curve on the output ramp (still exact destination)
In 1: type=input: target, Destination value
In 2: type=input: duration, Ramp time in SAMPLES
Return 1: Ramp, Output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete
Return 2: Notify, 1 When Ramp Reaches Destination (0 During Ramp)

entry.name: eviRampsmooth ( )
entry.description:
Reimplementation of MSP [rampsmooth~] algorithm, ramp times only update if input value changes. Exact destination ramps.
In 1: type=input: input, Value to filter
In 2: type=input: frampup, Ramp up time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: frampdown, Ramp down time in SAMPLES
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothed output, or target value if ramps are complete
Return 2: Notify, 1 When Ramp Reaches Destination (0 During Ramp)

entry.name: eviRampsmoothUpdate ( )
entry.description:
Reimplementation of MSP [rampsmooth~] algorithm, ramp times continuously update regardless of if input value changes. Exact destination ramps.
In 1: type=input: input, Value to filter
In 2: type=input: frampup, Ramp up time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: frampdown, Ramp down time in SAMPLES
Return 1: Smooth, Smoothed output, or target value if ramps are complete
Return 2: Notify, 1 When Ramp Reaches Destination (0 During Ramp)

entry.name: eviCurve ( )
entry.description:
Reimplementation of MSP [curve~] algorithm. Exact destination ramp. Note, this is expensive in gen~.
In 1: type=input: target, Destination value
In 2: type=input: duration, Ramp time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: curvature, Ramp curvature -1..1, 0==linear
Return 1: Ramp, Output ramp, or target value if ramp is complete
Return 2: Notify, 1 When Ramp Reaches Destination (0 During Ramp)

entry.name: likeAvactrol ( )
entry.description:
A digital model of a vactrol filter, quasi 'analog' in behaviour
In 1: type=input: V, Voltage
In 2: type=input: up, Up time in normalised values
In 3: type=input: down, Down time in normalised values
Return 1: Vactrol Envelope, This needs quite a lot of massaging to work well, see the 'evi_vactrol_shape.gendsp' reference page for details

entry.name: vactrolBuchla ( )
entry.description:
Vactrol time-domain behaviour filter. A basic not-really-a-model of the Perkin Elmer VTL5C3, the resistive part of a photoresistive opto-isolator. See the 'evi_vactrol.gendsp' reference page for more details
In 1: type=input: i, Impulse
In 2: type=param (optional): rise, default: 20,
In 3: type=param (optional): fall, default: 3000,
In 4: type=param (optional): base, default: 1000, Base frequency in Hz, should be in range 100..10000; default 1000 is the same as 'evi_vactrol_fix.gendsp'. Very powerful in changing shape of envelope curve and peak/trough of envelope.
Return 1: Vactrol Envelope, Output will behave similarly to the Buchla vactrol with correct settings of parameter values
